component.name: org.nuxeo.agentic.connectors.webhooks
component.documentation:
Outbound webhooks: a document event, on a document of a webhook's types, sent to the receiver the server names, signed, once its transaction has committed, in the background.
The server's configuration contributes a webhook here, in nxserver/config/: which events, on which types, with which of the document's properties. What each server sets, never a contribution: the receiver's address, nuxeo.agentic.webhooks.(the webhook's id).address, https only unless nuxeo.agentic.webhooks.(id).http.allowed is true; the secret each delivery is signed with, nuxeo.agentic.webhooks.(id).secret, at least 32 characters; and whether the address may be a private or loopback one, nuxeo.agentic.webhooks.(id).private.allowed. Without the address or the secret, the webhook sends nothing and keeps nothing.
A delivery is signed as the change events Nuxeo takes are: X-Nuxeo-Connector-Timestamp, -Nonce and -Signature, sha256= and the HMAC-SHA256 of the webhook's id, the timestamp and the nonce, each followed by a line feed, then the body. It is retried with a growing wait, then kept as a dead letter, which only an administrator lists (Webhook.Deliveries) and sends again (Webhook.Resend).

extension-point.name: webhooks
extension-point.documentation:
One webhook per element. Only id, at least one event and at least one type are required. The events are created, modified, transitioned (a lifecycle transition) and taskCompleted (a workflow task done on the document). A field names a document property, prefix:name, or ecm:currentLifeCycleState; file:content and files:files are refused.
created modified transitioned taskCompleted Claim
6 2000 10000
The payload is the delivery's id, the event, the document's id and type, and these fields, each under its name, and nothing else; a value that is not text, a number, a boolean, a date or a list of those is sent as null. maxAttempts is 1 to 10, 6 by default. The timeouts are in milliseconds, up to 10000 to connect and 30000 for the whole attempt. A webhook that fails a check is not registered, and the log says why. A later contribution with the same id replaces it whole, and enabled="false" removes it.
